page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-32 is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processors. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is configured at 64 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, complemented by hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA cryptographic instruction extensions. This instance configuration does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core scores reaching the upper quartile. Memory subsystem performance is a standout characteristic; the PassMark memory evaluation places the instance in the top tier, supported by 128.39 GB/sec large-block uncached read throughput. Cryptographic throughput is similarly elevated, posting strong results in PassMark CPU encryption tests. For computational tasks, the platform achieves solid performance in Clang software compilation and image processing, while also demonstrating top-tier text generation speeds for lightweight 135M parameter language models.

The 1:2 memory-to-core allocation provides an efficient resource balance for processing-dense environments where high memory footprints would represent idle overhead. Because storage is completely externalized and no GPUs are provisioned, operational costs are directly aligned with dedicated CPU execution. The c2d-highcpu-32 is effectively deployed for software build pipelines, image and video processing, batch computation, web serving fleets, and CPU-driven cryptographic operations.
